The Larkspur Archive is a digitized-collection platform for Bellweather
Books: scanning, OCR, searchable metadata, and an online viewer. The OCR
pipeline uses a remote OCR API over local OCR (decision d-004, informed by
the ocr-comparison notes); a later latency benchmark (s-006) showed archival
page scans running far below the assumed throughput, which sent Dev and
Silas back to preprocessing. The viewer is IIIF-based (decision d-011),
prototyped in s-010.

Team: Silas Brandt (data), June Park (interface), Dev Okonkwo (OCR pipeline),
Odessa Klein (user research). Rowan Ellery is the client sponsor; Quill &
Marrow advised the metadata descriptions. Mid-project review with Bellweather
is m-007.

As of mid-June the project is active: OCR continues at the corrected rate and
the IIIF viewer is in integration.

Context: Bellweather's archive scans number in the tens of thousands of
pages; OCR throughput sets the digitization schedule.

Options considered: local OCR on the studio's machines; a remote OCR API.

Decision: route Larkspur OCR through a remote API — roughly four times local
throughput at an absorbable per-page cost, informed by the ocr-comparison
benchmark notes.

Consequences: the digitization schedule holds; throughput is assumed to scale
linearly with scan volume. Later contradicted by the latency benchmark in
s-006, which found archival page scans far below the assumed rate.

Silas benchmarked the OCR pipeline against the ocr-comparison assumption: on
real archival page scans — foxed paper, old typefaces — throughput ran at
roughly forty percent of the assumed rate once image preprocessing landed.
The linearity assumption behind d-004 does not hold for archival material;
batching and preprocessing now set the schedule, not API capacity.

Mid-project review at Bellweather with Rowan's team: the OCR latency findings
(s-006) were walked through — archival scans run at roughly forty percent of
the assumed rate, so the digitization schedule stretches — and the IIIF
viewer direction (d-011, prototyped in s-010) was welcomed. Rowan asked for a
wallboard-style collection status page; June takes it.

final_answer:
**Larkspur OCR Story Synthesis**

**Original Assumption** (Decision d-004): The team chose a remote OCR API over local OCR, assuming it would deliver "roughly four times local throughput at an absorbable per-page cost" and that "throughput is assumed to scale linearly with scan volume" — this assumption underpinned the digitization schedule.

**Benchmark Finding** (Session s-006): Silas benchmarked the pipeline on real archival scans (foxed paper, old typefaces) and found throughput ran at "roughly forty percent of the assumed rate once image preprocessing landed." The linearity assumption failed for archival material: "batching and preprocessing now set the schedule, not API capacity."

**Schedule Consequence** (Meeting m-007): At the mid-project review with Bellweather, the team "walked through" the latency findings — "archival scans run at roughly forty percent of the assumed rate, so the digitization schedule stretches."
